steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: At the top of the file, import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState. This will allow you to use React components and state management.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing libraries for a project
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// No code yet — this is the first step.

// Import React and useState here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have import statements for React and useState at the top.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This sets up the foundation for building stateful components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StateMachineUI that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the StateMachineUI component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named StateMachineUI is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named StateMachineUI and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main component that will contain your state machine.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named exactly 'StateMachineUI' and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the correct name and returned a div element.

steps.title: Define the finite state machine states
steps.instruction: Inside your StateMachineUI component, create a constant object named 'states' that defines the possible UI states: IDLE, LOADING, SUCCESS, and ERROR.
steps.hint: Define an object with string values for each state. For example: const states = { IDLE: 'idle', LOADING: 'loading' }
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a 'states' object with four properties: IDLE, LOADING, SUCCESS, and ERROR, each with string values representing the state names.
successCriteria: A 'states' constant object is defined inside the component with IDLE, LOADING, SUCCESS, and ERROR properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the possible states for your finite state machine. This gives you clear, named states to work with throughout your UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined all four states: IDLE, LOADING, SUCCESS, and ERROR as properties of a 'states' object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a constant object named 'states' with properties for IDLE, LOADING, SUCCESS, and ERROR. Each property should have a string value representing that state.

steps.title: Initialize the current state
steps.instruction: Inside your StateMachineUI component, initialize a state variable called currentState using useState. Set its initial value to 'IDLE'.
steps.hint: Call useState with 'IDLE' as the initial argument, and destructure the returned array into currentState and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable currentState initialized to 'IDLE', ready to track the UI's current state.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with 'IDLE' as the initial value, and the returned array is destructured into currentState and a setter function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the currentState variable to track the UI's state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState with 'IDLE' as the initial value and destructuring the returned array into currentState and a setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Initialize a state variable called currentState with useState, starting with the value 'IDLE'.

steps.title: Create state transition functions
steps.instruction: Inside your StateMachineUI component, create three functions named goToLoading, goToSuccess, and goToError. Each function should call setCurrentState with the appropriate state value.
steps.hint: Define each function using arrow functions or function declarations. Inside each, call setCurrentState with the corresponding string: 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', or 'ERROR'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three transition functions are defined inside the component, each updating the state to a specific UI state.
successCriteria: Functions goToLoading, goToSuccess, and goToError are defined, each calling setCurrentState with the correct state string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the transition functions that will drive your state machine.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined some transition functions, but make sure you have all three: goToLoading, goToSuccess, and goToError.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition functions aren't defined correctly. Create three functions that update the currentState to 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', and 'ERROR'.

steps.title: Add a reset function
steps.instruction: Inside your StateMachineUI component, create a function named resetState that sets the current state back to 'IDLE'.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCurrentState with the initial state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A resetState function is defined in the component, ready to be used later.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named resetState that calls setCurrentState('IDLE').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the reset function. This will allow users to return the state machine to its starting point.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named resetState and it calls setCurrentState with 'IDLE'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset function isn't quite right. It should be named resetState and set the current state back to 'IDLE'.

steps.title: Add the component structure
steps.instruction: Return a main container div with a header and a content section from your component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with JSX that includes a div, a heading, and a section.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic UI structure with a container, header, and content section.
successCriteria: The component returns JSX containing a div with at least a header element and a section element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the basic UI structure. The component now returns a container with a header and content section.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component returns a div containing both a header (like h1) and a section element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component still returns null or an incomplete structure. Return a div with a header and a section.

steps.title: Display the current state
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the currentState value.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

tag and embed the currentState variable inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current state value (initially 'IDLE') in a paragraph.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the return statement that displays the currentState value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the current state value in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added a paragraph element with the currentState variable inside curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element displaying currentState is missing or incorrect. Check that you added

{currentState}

inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add state transition buttons
steps.instruction: Inside your component, add three buttons before the closing tag. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls setCurrentState with the appropriate state string: 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', and 'ERROR'. Label them 'Start Loading', 'Mark Success', and 'Mark Error' respectively.
steps.hint: Create <button> elements with onClick={() => setCurrentState('STATE_NAME')} and appropriate text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three buttons appear in the UI that, when clicked, will change the currentState to LOADING, SUCCESS, or ERROR.
successCriteria: Three <button> elements are added with onClick handlers calling setCurrentState with the correct state strings and appropriate labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added buttons that will trigger state transitions. Each button updates the currentState to a different UI state when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some buttons, but check that all three are present with the correct onClick handlers and labels: LOADING, SUCCESS, ERROR.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't set up correctly. Make sure you have three <button> elements with onClick handlers that call setCurrentState with the state strings 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', and 'ERROR'.

steps.title: Wire buttons to transition functions
steps.instruction: Add onClick handlers to each button that call the appropriate transition function.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on each button to call the corresponding transition function you created earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button to a handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each button will have an onClick handler that triggers the corresponding state transition when clicked.
successCriteria: All four buttons have onClick handlers that call the appropriate transition functions (transitionToLoading, transitionToSuccess, transitionToError, resetState).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired all buttons to their corresponding transition functions. Now clicking each button will change the state appropriately.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some onClick handlers, but not all buttons are wired yet. Make sure each button has an onClick handler that calls the correct transition function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons don't have onClick handlers yet. Add onClick attributes to each button that call the corresponding transition functions you created earlier.

steps.title: Add a reset button
steps.instruction: Add an onClick handler to the Reset button that calls the resetState function.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on the Reset button and set it to call resetState.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding onClick to a button
<button onClick={resetFunction}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Reset button will now trigger the resetState function when clicked, resetting the state machine to IDLE.
successCriteria: The Reset button has an onClick handler that calls resetState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Reset button is now wired to reset the state machine.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an onClick handler, but make sure it calls the resetState function correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Reset button still needs an onClick handler that calls resetState.

steps.title: Add conditional UI based on state
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add conditional rendering that displays different messages for each state. Use the currentState variable to show different UI content for 'IDLE', 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', and 'ERROR' states.
steps.hint: You can use if/else statements, switch statements, or ternary operators inside JSX to conditionally render different content based on currentState.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will now show different messages or content depending on which state the finite state machine is in, making the state changes visually apparent to the user.
successCriteria: Conditional rendering is implemented that displays different UI content for each possible state ('IDLE', 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', 'ERROR').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering that shows different UI content based on the current state. This completes your finite state machine UI implementation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some conditional logic, but make sure you handle all four states ('IDLE', 'LOADING', 'SUCCESS', 'ERROR') with appropriate UI content for each.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't working correctly. Make sure you're checking the currentState variable and rendering different content for each possible state value.
